newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: El Salvador guns-for-goods program called success.
newsitem.headline: El Salvador guns-for-goods program called success.

text.p: Many Salvadorans have been trading in assault rifles, grenades and rocket launchers for consumer goods in a programme aimed at reducing violence in this Central American country, organisers said on Monday.

"We're content because the people have responded by bringing in a large number of war weapons," David Gutierrez, chief of the Patriotic Movement Against Delinquency, which devised the "Guns for Goods" programme, told a news conference.

Gutierrez said in the first week the programme collected 150 rifles, mostly M-16 and AK-47 assault rifles, along with 81 handguns, five rocket-launchers and 35 grenades plus a wide array of dynamite and C4 explosives.

Thousands of Salvadorans have kept high-powered weapons since a 12-year-long civil war that killed an estimated 75,000 people ended in 1992. The government estimates 300,000 military arms were left in civilian hands, of which 140,000 have since been recovered.

Guns for Goods, financed by a group of business leaders, a local Rotary Club and the Roman Catholic Church, was intended to get poor people to give up their arms in exchange for coupons to buy consumer goods such as food and clothes.

For each handgun, participants receive a coupon worth the equivalent of $172, while each rifle brings a coupon worth the equivalent of $345. The programme will continue each weekend until Dec. 15 with collection sites at Roman Catholic churches in major cities.
Anonymity for the participants is guaranteed and the Legislative Assembly passed a law that permits carrying war weapons to the collection sites.
